hints.title: Unifying Incoming and Outgoing Calls
hints.text: A person participates in a call as either caller or recipient. Construct an undirected view of all calls with caller_id, recipient_id, and call_time.

hints.title: Ranking Chronologically Per Day
hints.text: Use row_number partitioned by user_id and call date ordered by call_time ascending (to find first) and descending (to find last).

hints.title: Checking Partner Equality
hints.text: Find users where the other party in the first call equals the other party in the last call on the same date.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH AllCalls AS (
    SELECT caller_id AS user_id, recipient_id AS other_id, call_time FROM Calls
    UNION ALL
    SELECT recipient_id AS user_id, caller_id AS other_id, call_time FROM Calls
),
RankedCalls AS (
    SELECT
        user_id,
        other_id,
        DATE(call_time) AS call_date,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id, DATE(call_time) ORDER BY call_time ASC) AS rnk_first,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id, DATE(call_time) ORDER BY call_time DESC) AS rnk_last
    FROM AllCalls
)
SELECT DISTINCT
    r1.user_id
FROM RankedCalls r1
JOIN RankedCalls r2
    ON r1.user_id = r2.user_id
    AND r1.call_date = r2.call_date
    AND r1.rnk_first = 1
    AND r2.rnk_last = 1
WHERE r1.other_id = r2.other_id;
```

complexity.time: O(C log C) where C is total calls
complexity.space: O(C) space for symmetric calls view
variables: C: number of call records in Calls table
complexity.notes: Symmetric call union with ROW_NUMBER() window ranks.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Considering only outgoing calls ignores calls received by a user.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dual ROW_NUMBER window evaluations isolate earliest and latest call partners per day.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle both incoming and outgoing directions and identical partner verification.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def same_day_calls(calls: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    c1 = calls.rename(columns={'caller_id': 'user_id', 'recipient_id': 'other_id'})
    c2 = calls.rename(columns={'recipient_id': 'user_id', 'caller_id': 'other_id'})
    all_calls = pd.concat([c1, c2])
    all_calls['date'] = pd.to_datetime(all_calls['call_time']).dt.date
    all_calls = all_calls.sort_values('call_time')
    
    first = all_calls.groupby(['user_id', 'date']).first().reset_index()
    last = all_calls.groupby(['user_id', 'date']).last().reset_index()
    
    m = pd.merge(first, last, on=['user_id', 'date'])
    same = m[m['other_id_x'] == m['other_id_y']]
    return same[['user_id']].drop_duplicates()
solutions.approach: Symmetric concatenation and first/last aggregation in pandas
